name: Workers SDK
tagline: Wrangler and the toolchain for Cloudflare Workers.
hook: States that copied values go stale, and points at the config that defines them instead.
summary: Opens with a rule about its own maintenance, then covers commands, a task-to-location table, cross-tool development, and testing conventions. Subsystem detail is delegated to per-package files.

techniques.title: A stated policy against copying
techniques.body: The second sentence of the file rules out copying details into it, naming versions, rule lists and counts as the things that go stale. Later sections apply it: the root package file is named as authoritative for scripts, and a validation command replaces a duplicated list of enforced lint rules.
techniques.quote:
Prefer authoritative configuration and documentation over copying
details into this file: copied versions, rule lists, and counts become stale.

techniques.title: A table indexed by task, not by directory
techniques.body: Fourteen rows map a thing the agent might be asked to do onto the location that handles it, with a note on each. The first column is the task rather than the path, so the table is read by intent.

techniques.title: A rule about which layer a feature belongs in
techniques.body: Three tools consume the same development platform, so a feature is stated to be incomplete if it only works through one of them. Implementation goes in the shared layer wherever possible, with the integration layers kept thin, and intentional gaps documented in the pull request.
techniques.quote:
A development feature is not complete merely
because it works through one of them.

techniques.title: Package files kept current in the same change
techniques.body: Packages carry their own instruction files, and the agent is directed to read the closest applicable one before making changes and to update it in the same change when the change makes it inaccurate. The division of content between the root file and package files is stated.

techniques.title: One security rule with its linter
techniques.body: Shell commands may not be built from interpolated or concatenated untrusted input, and the custom lint rule that enforces it is named.

steal: Put the anti-drift rule in the file itself. Naming versions, rule lists and counts as things not to copy is what keeps it from rotting.
Index your repo map by task rather than by directory. Agents arrive with an intent, not a path.
If several tools consume one platform, state which layer a feature belongs in and that one consumer is not done.
Require the package instruction file to be updated in the same change that makes it wrong.
